sm_github.json:10:          "description": "RULE ORDER (dmtools-agents#682, live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03 23:05–23:57, still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22): runs FIRST, ahead of merge-validated AND sweep-stale-validating (whose relative order is a documented #637 invariant — this rule preserves it by prefixing, never interleaving). A cancelled required check is never a verdict: the sweep skips cancelled conclusions by design and fail-validation owns red, so this rule cannot fight them — it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, it only re-runs GitHub Actions runs. GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). CANCELLED is read with branch-protection semantics: the LATEST check run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp does NOT act (#695 review fix). NOT failure — failure paths exist; NOT pending-with-active-runs — the localAction probes every run on the head (hasActiveDispatchedRun pattern widened to all events) and skips while anything is in flight. localAction rerun_cancelled_checks re-runs (gh run rerun) the latest attempt-1 cancelled run per required context and posts a once-per-head marker comment citing the evidence — ONLY when the rerun set covers every cancelled context (a partial set defers the marker so the uncovered contexts stay actionable; #695). BEHIND (silent-update refreshes the head) and DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it) are excluded, and agent:rework defers to the rework leg. limit 2: the observed death takes two PRs per wave (fa#1202+#1203 in one 36-second push wave). gh-755 SPLIT (owner directive 2026-10-05 'cancelled must re-run'): machine-authored armed heads moved to rerun-any-cancelled-checks — the ANY-cancelled sibling DIRECTLY BELOW, whose rerun set is a superset of this rule's (a cancelled required context is included in 'any'); this rule keeps the required contexts for GUEST heads only (query.notMachine — the twins are author-disjoint, exactly one rerun rule matches any PR, no double rerun, no marker interference; with no machineAuthor configured notMachine is inert and this rule again covers every PR, so the coverage degrades to the pre-gh-755 behavior, never below it). Guests keep the NAMED-context scope deliberately: re-running the deployment's own branch protection on a guest head is the machine's business, a guest's foreign CI is not.",
sm_github.json:38:          "description": "gh-755 (owner directive 2026-10-05: 'если что-то канселится — надо повторно запускать' — a CANCELLED run is not a verdict; rework legs on cancellations burn tokens for nothing): the ANY-cancelled twin of rerun-cancelled-checks, sitting IMMEDIATELY after it (the #682 rule-order invariant stands: rerun-cancelled-checks stays FIRST; the #637 invariant is untouched — this prefix never interleaves merge-validated / sweep-stale-validating). Live gap (2026-10-05, dmtools-agents PRs #752/#753): the kicker's sm-liveness + docs-freshness push runs ended cancelled/failed after the 15m verdict window — the named rule only re-runs the deployment's branch-protection requiredContexts, so every OTHER workflow's cancelled context (kicker sm-liveness / head-completeness, docs-freshness, CodeQL, …) had NO remedy: the head stayed BLOCKED/UNSTABLE, the merge stalled, and the fail-validation legs burned rework on the rollup mess. This rule re-runs ANY check context whose LATEST check run on the head reads CANCELLED (rule.anyCancelled — no name list; the localAction scans the whole check-runs rollup). Branch-protection semantics preserved (#695): the LATEST run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp never acts, a fresh cancel over a stale green does. MACHINE-AUTHOR-ONLY (query.prMachineAuthor, fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured — in that deployment this rule is inert and the named rule covers everyone): a guest head's non-required cancels are the guest's own CI, not ours to re-run; the machine re-runs only its own heads. notMachine on the named rule makes the twins author-disjoint — exactly one rerun rule matches any PR, so the once-per-head markers never interfere and no run is ever rerun twice. Same guards as the named rule: the localAction probes every run on the head (hasActiveHeadRun, all events) and skips while anything is in flight (an in-flight run re-stamps the contexts itself); rerun targets are the newest attempt-1 cancelled run per cancelled context (run_attempt > 1 already fired the remedy — no loop); a partial coverage set defers the once-per-head marker so uncovered contexts stay actionable (#695); BEHIND (silent-update refreshes the head) and DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it) are excluded; agent:rework in notLabels defers to the rework leg. FAIL-VALIDATION PARITY (gh-755 ask 2): the fail path's arm-time red-verdict probe (headHasRealFailure) treats a cancelled-only rollup as no-verdict — a PR whose only red is a cancelled check gets a rerun, never an agent:rework arm. limit 2: parity with the named rule (the observed death takes two PRs per wave).",
sm_github.json:114:          "description": "Validated-but-stale: armed (ai_validating) + validation concluded but BASE MOVED (BEHIND only). BLOCKED must NOT unarm: since #483 BLOCKED is a real verdict, and on a freshly armed head BLOCKED simply means 'required checks pending' — unarming there races validate-armed in the SAME tick and deadlocks the PR forever (live: fa pr-762 armed at 08:25:37, unarmed 08:25:58 by the BLOCKED match, re-armed next tick, loop). silent-update-behind excludes ai_validating and merge-validated needs CLEAN, so without this unarm a genuinely moved base still deadlocks (live: fa pr-744) — BEHIND-only keeps that recovery and stops the self-inflicted one. gh-751 VERDICT-AWARE STRIP (live: fa #1295 — the arm was stripped FIVE times in one day with zero latches, [ai_validating]→[]→[ai_validating] yo-yo under a saturated CI queue): every main merge made the armed head BEHIND and this strip DISCARDED the head's ALREADY-CONCLUDED green verdict — it lost the race to the strip (merge-validated needs CLEAN; validated-green sits later and excludes pr_approved), silent-update refreshed, validate-fresh re-armed, the next merge re-struck: a full re-validation per main merge. The action now probes the head's dispatched validation runs before stripping: a GREEN run ANYWHERE on the head latches ai_validated instead of the bare unarm — not only the newest run: gh-748 showed two workflow_dispatch runs landing on ONE head seconds apart, and the latch consumer (validate-armed's skipIfValidatedHead → hasSuccessfulDispatchedRun) accepts any completed-green run on the head, so the strip consumes that same facet (complete_validation parity — sweep_stale_validation's success-branch shape; the latch excludes the PR from validate-fresh, and validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head so the merge window re-flows without new CI); only when NO green run exists on the head (red / absent / in-flight / cancelled-only) does the bare unarm stand (refresh + re-validate recovery).",
sm_github.json:131:          "description": "RULE ORDER (dmtools-agents#637 aftermath, live fa pr-1174 2026-10-03): this rule MUST run before sweep-stale-validating — the 15-min staleness sweep eats every arm before the merge can consume it whenever the tick cadence slips past 15 min (night kicker slippage), looping arm→sweep→arm on a green merge-ready head. GitHub PR: validation green + CLEAN -> squash-merge (merge_pr verifies the sticky pr_approved latch on the PR; an un-approved green head latches ai_validated instead — see merge_pr). FIFO drain (#687). PRIORITY TIERS (owner directive 2026-10-08, amends the 2026-09-22 FIFO rule): the merge pick is FIFO WITHIN a tier — a priority_blocker merges FIRST, ahead of older mediums (this limit-1 pick shares validate-armed's tier-aware sort in queryPrs; a preemption logs a 🥇 line in the tick log), priority_low SINKS below all mediums, and a PR with NO priority label is medium (the priority_medium label is NOT required to exist). Carrier: the label may sit on the PR OR its linked issue — either counts. Label NAMES configurable per project via .dmtools/config.js smPriorityLabels (defaults blocker/medium/low = priority_blocker/priority_medium/priority_low; absent mapping entries degrade to the defaults).",
sm_github.json:150:          "description": "RULE ORDER (owner directive 2026-10-04 'red yields the slot', live fa 11:0x: #1194 held ai_validating through repeated reds while #1215..#1223 sat FIFO-queued 40+ min): this rule MUST run BEFORE validate-armed — the unarm below frees the limit-1 mutex and (with the openPrs ioCache drop in the action) the arm rule's later query in the SAME tick sees the freed slot and arms the NEXT oldest approved PR immediately. Previously fail-validation ran after validate-armed: the arm rule scanned the still-occupied mutex every tick and the slot stayed hostage until the failed PR's rework cycle re-armed it. #637 rule-order invariant preserved: rerun-cancelled-checks stays first (#682/gh-682), and merge-validated still runs before sweep-stale-validating. GitHub PR: validation CI red on the head -> unarm ai_validating, report (with the 🔴 red-head counter marker — the validate_pr arm side skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds), requeue agent:rework on the linked issue. pr_approved is STICKY (owner rule 2026-09): the reworked head re-validates and merges without a re-review — no token burn on review legs. GUEST PRs (gh-757, live fa#1286: the 2026-10-04 guest validation-red arm spent an AI rework leg on a vendor PR): report + validation_failed PARK only — auto-rework is machine-author-ONLY (owner rule 2026-09-21 reaffirmed); the guest's own push clears the park (#633 RESET) and validation re-runs, and a HUMAN can still arm agent:rework manually on any PR (rework-on-label). Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): latch/unlatch verdicts in waves — pure label writes, nothing serial. gh-832 CONVERGENCE PARK (live fa #1453, 2026-10-10: 12 dispatch→red→unarm→rearm cycles on an unchanged approved head, 5 reds in a row, window idle 3.5h, no park, no comment): repeated red verdicts must never loop — the fail path counts CONSECUTIVE concluded-red dispatched runs on the unchanged head from the head's own run list (a green run breaks the streak, a head move resets it by construction, cancelled is never a verdict) and at jobParams.redHeadParkCap (default 2) PARKS validation_failed with a report naming the failing job(s) + the failed-run link. The parked PR leaves validate-armed's FIFO (notLabels excludes it) — NO third dispatch. Machine PRs keep the rework arm (routing unchanged) and exit the park via the gh-750 machine self-clear / #633 RESET probes on the next head; guests keep the red-1 park. jobParams.redHeadParkCap=false disables the park (the 🔴 marker audit trail and the 3-red arm-side skip are untouched).",
sm_github.json:164:          "description": "Stale-arm sweeper (live: fa #999 — ai_validating held 7h with a CONCLUDED green CI and no verdict consumed; the ai_validating mutex stayed held forever. unarm-stale-validation covers BEHIND only). ai_validating + the head's dispatched validation run CONCLUDED (success or failure — CANCELLED is never a verdict) more than staleMinutes (15) ago, arm never consumed → unarm. Success side: unarm + re-latch ai_validated (complete_validation parity — the merge window re-flows; validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head). Failure side: the standard fail path (report + machine-only rework re-arm). Fresh conclusions (<15 min) never sweep: the check-visibility/verdict race window — the same-tick verdict rules (merge-validated / fail-validation / validated-green) own those. BEHIND excluded: unarm-stale-validation owns the moved-base recovery. gh-821 ZOMBIE side (live: fa #1443, 2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z — the dispatched run concluded CANCELLED in the gh-748 kicker/dispatch race, this sweep kept the arm ('no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays') and four validated PRs deferred on the ai_validating mutex for ~2h until a manual gh workflow run ci.yml): a CANCELLED-only head or a head with NO dispatched run at all is a ZOMBIE — the arm holds the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it. Past the 15-min visibility grace (probe.active still reads 'running' inside it, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes) the liveness classification (js/common/validationLiveness.js) re-dispatches validation the SAME TICK — release the slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (a LIVE run now backs the mutex; no parallel validations) — logging '🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N'. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour (jobParams.zombieRedispatchMinMs, default 3600000), bookkept as marker comments (🔄 zombie re-dispatch <sha> — zombie N/cap at <iso>, the red-head carrier); 3 re-dispatches in a row on the same head (jobParams.zombieRedispatchCap, default 3) park validation_failed + explanatory comment — fail-closed, a new push (new head SHA) restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes. A live run keeps the arm exactly as before (AC3 — healthy flow untouched).",

sm_github.json:182:          "description": "Every open non-draft PR behind main gets a silent branch refresh with the workflow token (pushes trigger no workflows, so freshness is free); validating PRs are excluded so the validation head never moves mid-run. mergeState is BEHIND only: the prStatus deterministic override computes BEHIND from base freshness (immune to the REST BEHIND/BLOCKED flip-flop this rule used to paper over with both values), and BLOCKED is now a REAL verdict (fresh head, required checks pending/red) — updating those would no-op-clone every pending PR on every tick. Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the LAST SUBSTANTIVE commit (machine-authored merges of main walked back past, dmtools-agents#681) is a NON-machine push NEWER than the park, so the SM's own silent-updates — bot merges or re-arms — never clear a red guest's park. Machine-authored PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads; the label's SET rules are guest-gated — legacy parks predate that). MACHINE SELF-CLEAR (gh-750, owner directive 2026-10-05): a MACHINE-authored parked PR — legacy residue like fa#1227, the label predates this guest-only contract — clears when the current head's check rollup is GREEN or the head moved past the park carrying no red verdict of its own (probe failures keep the park, fail closed); guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior.",
sm_github.json:282:          "description": "Dead-zone fix (live: fa pr-922, 2026-09-26 — frozen in ai_validating for hours, ticks processed 0): the armed head's dispatched CI run was LOST (racing dispatch canceled by concurrency, or the gh workflow run CLI call failed silently — dispatchCiWorkflow cannot throw). Every existing check is green, but the required CI check is ABSENT from the head, so the rollup reads 'green' while REST mergeState stays BLOCKED. No rule matched: revalidate-armed wants checks=none, merge-validated wants CLEAN, fail-validation wants red, unarm-stale wants BEHIND. 'green' + not-CLEAN here means the arm is stale and the CI verdict is missing — re-dispatch (validate_pr's duplicate-dispatch guard skips if a run is already landing; the skipIfGreenCi flag stops the loop when a completed green CI run already covers the head and the blocker is some other workflow's required check). Armed+green+CLEAN must NOT match — that is merge-validated's merge — hence CLEAN is excluded. MUTEX with mutexExcludeSelf (multi-arm leak fix, live: fa 2026-09-26 — 7 approved PRs armed at once): same self-block reason as revalidate-armed made this rule ship mutex-less, and the same false singleton assumption let it feed the +1-arm-per-tick leak. The exclude-self mutex defers the candidate only while ANOTHER approved PR holds ai_validating; with the invariant restored this rule fires exactly on the one armed approved PR and never arms a second. gh-837: same mutexMax relaxation as validate-armed — with the parallel-validation knob active the exclude-self form still lets every self-holding candidate drain, and a non-holder defers only once OTHER approved arms reach the cap.",
sm_github.json:315:          "description": "GitHub PR: head with no CONCLUDED validation (checks 'none' — fresh push, no CI — or 'pending' — the dispatch bridge's waiting check runs; pushes fire no CI) -> dispatch the CI workflow on the head + ai_validating marker. OWNER RULE (2026-09-23, validation economy): validate ONCE per PR — the first green is the ticket to review; after it the ai_validated latch excludes the PR here, silent-update keeps it fresh (no re-validation on refresh), and the single pre-merge validation lives in validate-armed (post-approve, current head). Red heads repeat this rule only after a NEW push clears the red. chore:pin PRs (factory lockstep bumps) are exempt: the factory suite gates them before the cut, and the next real PR validates the pinned content via silent-update. DELIBERATELY author-agnostic (gh-757 review): validating external/vendor PRs is the sanctioned prerequisite for the owner-ruled external review flow (review-external-once needs checks green, and pushes fire no CI) and for the guest sticky-park contract — only the auto-REWORK arm is machine-author-gated (fail_validation), never the validation dispatch itself.",
sm_github.json:337:          "description": "Post-dev dead-zone fix (gh-759, live fa 2026-10-06: PRs #1305/#1306/#1309/#1311/#1312 — five fresh machine PRs BLOCKED with ZERO labels for hours, each unblocked by hand-arming ai_validating + dispatching CI; agents #756 / fa #1295 / fa #1304 are the same class patched by hand the same day). The dev leg completes (issue ai_developed + status:In Review) and the fresh head IMMEDIATELY carries GREEN check runs from the deployment's ambient workflows (fa: kicker sm-liveness/head-completeness, CodeQL, the analyze suite) — while the DISPATCH-ONLY validation CI (jobParams.ciWorkflow, no push trigger) has never been ordered. The rollup reads 'green', so validate-fresh (checks [none, pending]) never matches; every verdict/re-dispatch rule needs ai_validating or pr_approved, and the PR carries zero labels — nothing ever arms validation and the PR dead-locks. This rule is the UN-ARMED twin of revalidate-armed-green (gh-922): rollup green + none of ai_validating/pr_approved/ai_validated/chore:pin/validation_failed → validate_pr probes the head for a dispatched CI run — none (or cancelled-only) → dispatch + arm ai_validating; a completed GREEN run → skipIfGreenCi skips (the blocker is another workflow's required check — re-running loops forever). Disjoint from validate-fresh by construction (none/pending vs green) and from every verdict rule by labels; notMergeState excludes BEHIND (silent-update refreshes first) and DIRTY (conflict-rework). Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ # gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. # gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# gh-842: [GOAL] Cancelled-run check-run zombies hold the merge gate BLOCKED forever (live: fa #1457 ~2h; in_progress ghosts from a cancelled queued run)

## Description

## Goal

A merge gate must never be held by check-run zombies: when a dispatched CI run is CANCELLED while queued (gh-748 twin-guard or otherwise), its registered check-runs can stay `in_progress` forever — the branch gate takes the LATEST check-run per context and waits on a dead run indefinitely.

## Subject

Merge-gate hygiene in the SM tick. Live instance fa #1457, head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10 ~14:30→16:00Z: "Quality gate"/"Binaries smoke gate"/"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" each carried an `in_progress` check-run whose run no longer exists (html_url unresolvable) PLUS terminal entries from run 38057801418 (green, 13:58). mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED for ~2h with an otherwise-mergeable head (pr_approved + green validation + 0 unresolved threads). The tick never re-dispatched (its rollup read green), so the window idled until an operator nudged a fresh dispatch (16:0xZ).

## Capability surface

- Detection: merge-validated (or a pre-merge sweep) lists head check-runs; an `in_progress`/`queued` check-run whose run_id 404s or whose run is `cancelled` ⇒ zombie.
- Action: count the context as ABSENT (gh-921 semantics) and re-dispatch validation on that head (limit 1/tick) instead of treating the rollup as green.
- Optional belt: on cancel paths, post a check-run conclusion `cancelled` for the contexts the cancelled run had registered (if the API allows) so the gate never waits on ghosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #1457 timeline — the zombie is detected ≤1 tick after creation and a re-dispatch fires (no operator nudge).
2. AC2: a genuinely in-progress run (runner alive) is never disturbed.
3. AC3: no double-dispatch (existing skipIfGreenCi/run-landing probes still apply).
4. AC4: live soak — zero operator nudges needed for gate-zombie class over a week.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for zombie classification (run 404 / cancelled / stale >N min with no runner).
- L2: replay the real #1457 check-run timeline.
- L3 (live): observed after ship.

## Non-goals

- Changing the gh-748 cancel decision itself.
- The red-loop park (#832) — separate.

## References

- Instance: fa #1457 head 7d00a1b2, 2026-10-10; operator nudge ~16:0xZ.
- Family: gh-748 (cancel twins), gh-921/922 (missing checks), #832 (red convergence).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…
